description:
THE FROST Cold plasma by skinlab. is the professional electro-cosmetic device developed for the 2026 model year, combining cold plasma, warm plasma and ozone plasma technology in a single unit. The plasma is generated from high-purity argon gas.

Its goal is to visibly improve skin condition without incisions or bleeding, designed exclusively for cosmetic and aesthetic use.

The device is not a medical device. Cold plasma treatments fall within the competence of beauticians; the deeper-acting warm plasma functions require appropriate professional competence. Complete legal documentation is included with every unit.

science.headline: How does cold plasma work?
science.subtitle: What happens in the treatment head and on the skin – explained simply, so you can explain it to your clients too.

features.title: Plasma from argon – and why doesn't it burn?
features.description:
A high-frequency electric field of approx. 40 kHz is generated in THE FROST's treatment head while a controlled amount of high-purity argon gas flows through it. The accelerated electrons collide with the argon atoms and “knock” electrons out of them. This is how plasma is created: a partially ionised gas containing positive ions, free electrons, excited atoms and reactive molecules.

Why isn't it hot? The energy is carried almost exclusively by the extremely light electrons, while the heavy gas particles barely heat up. This is what is known as non-equilibrium plasma: the beam is only approx. 30–40 °C, so it is biologically active yet causes no thermal damage.

approx. 40 kHzargon, min. 99.6%approx. 30–40 °C beam

features.title: What does plasma do to the skin?
features.description:
It is not heat that does the work, but chemistry and biophysics. When the plasma beam leaves the treatment head, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS and RNS) are formed from the oxygen and nitrogen molecules in the air. In the right dose, these are also the body's own signalling molecules – and they account for most of cold plasma's biological effect:
Disinfection – damages the cell walls and proteins of bacteria, reducing, for example, the amount of acne bacteria (Cutibacterium acnes) and fungi
Anti-inflammatory effect – reduces redness, so it works well after acne and – with the right parameters – on sensitive skin too
Cell activation – the metabolism of existing cells and their communication with one another become more efficient
Regeneration – supports fibroblast function and collagen production; the device does not “produce” collagen, it activates the skin's own processes
Microcirculation – thanks to the vasodilating effect of nitric oxide, local blood circulation and oxygen supply may improve
Active ingredient penetration – the skin's permeability temporarily increases, so water-based serums are utilised better (the extent depends on the formula and the condition of the skin)

features.title: Why argon and not air?
features.description:
Some plasma systems simply ionise the ambient air. However, the composition of air changes constantly – humidity, temperature and impurities all affect it – so the plasma generated from it is less uniform too. Argon is an inert noble gas: its composition is constant, it does not react with the skin on its own, and it ionises predictably. That is why THE FROST produces nearly identical plasma in every treatment.
More stable plasma arc
More even energy transfer
More precisely controllable treatment
Fewer unwanted by-products
Reproducible treatment results
The manufacturer recommends using argon of at least 99.6% purity – lower-purity industrial gas can impair plasma stability and the operation of the device.

faq.question: What is the difference between THE FROST 2026 and the earlier THE FROST model?
faq.answer: The 2026 model features enhanced energy regulation and refined treatment heads that enable even more precise treatments. The core 9 functions and three plasma technologies remain, but the treatment experience and effectiveness have been further improved.

faq.question: Can I legally use the device as a beautician?
faq.answer: For cold plasma treatments, yes: these fall within the competence of beauticians, and we provide complete legal documentation with every device purchased from us. The warm plasma (thermoplasma) functions, however, are deeper, heat-based treatments that are not unambiguously within beautician competence in Hungary – they are recommended primarily for medical-aesthetic settings, used by practitioners with appropriate qualifications.

faq.question: What is the difference between cold plasma and warm plasma?
faq.answer: Cold plasma does not heat the skin and acts only on the skin surface and in the upper layers: it is painless, causes no wounding, scabbing or peeling, and involves no healing time. It is recommended for acne-prone, inflamed and sensitive skin, for soothing the skin, for regeneration and for active ingredient delivery. Warm plasma uses heat to stimulate deeper layers: after the treatment, healing time has to be expected (redness, peeling and scabbing may occur), and aftercare and increased sun protection are required.

faq.question: What is the difference between cold plasma and a conventional plasma pen?
faq.answer: A conventional plasma pen (fibroblast) creates burn points on the skin, which is painful and involves significant recovery time. Cold plasma technology, by contrast, is non-invasive, painless and has no downtime.

faq.question: What skin problems is it suitable for?
faq.answer: Cold plasma is particularly effective for acne-prone, inflamed skin, for soothing sensitive, problematic skin, for improving scars and skin irregularities, for skin with pigmentation spots, as a complement to anti-aging treatments, and for promoting better absorption of active ingredients. The Scalp Plasma head can also be used for scalp treatments. Ozone plasma is ideal for inflammatory skin conditions, while thermoplasma is ideal primarily for firming and anti-aging purposes.

faq.question: Does cold plasma have an anti-aging effect?
faq.answer: Yes, but not through heat-based firming – rather through a regenerating effect that improves skin quality: it improves the skin's oxygen supply, supports cell renewal, refines the skin surface and indirectly supports collagen function. For anti-aging purposes, the Derma Plasma (skin rejuvenation, pore refinement) and Stamp Plasma (skin texture, firmness) heads are the most important, while Jet Plasma enhances the effect by delivering serums, peptides and vitamins. Ideal combination: Derma or Stamp Plasma + Jet Plasma.

faq.question: Is the treatment painful?
faq.answer: Cold plasma treatment is painless: most clients feel mild warmth, tingling or a refreshing sensation, even on sensitive skin, and no anaesthesia is needed. Thermoplasma works with heat, so a stronger warm sensation may occur there.

faq.question: Is there healing time after the treatment?
faq.answer: Not after cold plasma: the client can return to their daily routine immediately, and peeling, wounds or bleeding are not typical. With warm plasma treatments, however, healing time has to be expected – redness, peeling and scabbing may occur – and aftercare and increased sun protection are required.

faq.question: How soon are results visible, and how many treatments are needed?
faq.answer: Many clients notice fresher, clearer skin after the very first treatment. For lasting results, a course of treatments is recommended depending on the condition of the skin, and it can also be booked occasionally for maintenance and a refresh.

faq.question: Can it be combined with other cosmetic treatments?
faq.answer: Yes, it is highly recommended: cold plasma complements facial treatments, active ingredient delivery and anti-aging protocols well, because it disinfects, soothes and helps active ingredients work better. That is why it is worth applying the serum immediately after the plasma treatment.

faq.question: Is it suitable for all skin types?
faq.answer: For most skin types, yes. Before the first treatment it is always worth holding a short consultation where you assess the condition of the skin and choose the right treatment mode. Contraindications and safety rules are covered in detail during the device operator training.

faq.question: What gas does the device use?
faq.answer: THE FROST generates its plasma from high-purity argon gas. The manufacturer recommends using argon of at least 99.6% purity: lower-purity industrial gases may contain more oxygen, nitrogen or other impurities, which impairs plasma stability and the operation of the device.

faq.question: How quickly does THE FROST 2026 pay for itself?
faq.answer: Cold plasma treatment prices typically range from 15,000 to 35,000 Ft. With 3-5 clients per day, the device generally pays for itself within 2-4 months. Use our ROI calculator for precise calculations!

faq.question: What training comes with the device?
faq.answer: One-day intensive operator training within officially registered adult education, free with device purchase. The training covers all 9 functions, treatment protocols, and includes practical treatments. An official B-number certificate is issued.
